references.text: God tells Jacob that nations and a community of nations shall come from him, and that kings shall proceed from his loins. This directly reflects the promise of fruitfulness, nations, and kings given to Abraham.

Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith and preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham: "In you all the families of the earth shall be blessed." This shows the spiritual fulfillment of the promise that Abraham would become the father of many nations.
God's promise to establish David's lineage forever and build his throne from generation to generation can be seen as a fulfillment of the promise that kings would come from Abraham's line.
God's original promise to Abraham to make him a great nation and bless him lays the foundation for the expanded promise that he will be exceedingly fruitful and become many peoples.
God promises that Sarah shall be the mother of nations, and that kings of peoples shall descend from her, which elaborates and specifies the promise concerning kings and nations.
Jacob recounts God's promise to make him fruitful and numerous and into a community of peoples, showing the continuation of Abraham's promise of fruitfulness and nations through his descendants.
Uses Abraham's covenant words about fruitfulness as a prophetic guarantee for the restoration of the nation Israel in Leviticus.
Prophetic renewal of Abraham's covenant promise of fruitfulness as part of God's plan for restoration in Ezekiel.
Retelling of Abraham's covenant to Isaac, confirming the promise of numerous descendants and lands.
Extends the promise of fruitfulness and peoples to Ishmael in the same chapter, showing the breadth of Abraham's blessing.
Blessing to Jacob that directly repeats Abraham's covenant words, confirming that the promise of peoples is transferred to him.
Direct quote/allusion to Abraham's covenant in Hebrews confirming God's faithfulness to the promise of making him numerous.
